papers.title: SkeinDB: Cell-Interned MVCC and Query-Scoped Delta Responses for HTTP-Native Database Caching
papers.abstract: Modern web applications (dashboards, software-as-a-service (SaaS) admin consoles, multi-tenant portals) often rely on aggressive polling of list queries. This produces high fan-out read traffic, in which successive query results are frequently identical or differ only slightly. Today, HTTP caches and application-layer proxies (content delivery networks (CDNs), reverse proxies, Redis) can reduce traffic, but they operate without database-native knowledge of query dependencies, row versioning, or result-set diffs. SkeinDB is a single-binary database engine scaffold that makes HTTP cache semantics first-class database primitives. It unifies three mechanisms: (i) cell-interned MVCC using content-addressed ValueIDs to deduplicate repeated cell values, (ii) dependency-derived ETags that enable sound conditional reads (HTTP If-None-Match/304) for rows and queries, and (iii) QueryPatch, a query-scoped delta response that transmits only the changes needed to update a previously seen result window. An adaptive reference planner guarantees that deduplication never regresses storage (R ≥ 1.0 by construction). Across six datasets, cell interning provides 0–82% storage savings, while QueryPatch reduces response bytes by 23–99.9% depending on change rate and window size.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Imperfect-Information Card Games:A Survey Using DouDiZhu as Benchmark
papers.abstract: Imperfect-information games (IIGs), characterized by hidden information and multi-agent interactions, present significant challenges for decision-making and reflect real-world scenarios such as negotiations and strategic planning. Among IIGs, imperfect-information card games (IICGs) form an important subclass due to their different rules, diverse strategic structures, and multi-agent interactions. However, most existing reviews on IIGs focus on general multi-agent learning, paying little attention to IICGs as a distinct and strategically rich subclass. DouDiZhu is an emerging topic in AI research for IICGs because of its asymmetric three-player roles, large state-action space, and complex strategic interactions. Recent research on DouDiZhu has explored a variety of approaches, including search-based methods (e.g., MCTS), deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods (e.g., DQN, DMC, PPO), and hybrid approaches that integrate learning, search, and opponent modeling. However, despite this progress, existing literature remains fragmented and lacks a systematic synthesis. To fill this gap, this survey positions DouDiZhu as a representative testbed for IICGs. It provides a comprehensive review and categorization of existing AI methods, analyzing their strengths and limitations, highlighting trends, and comparing performance against available baselines. The survey also identifies open challenges and future directions, including generalization beyond standard rules, unified bidding and playing, continual learning, and standardized evaluation. These challenges and directions guide future research and support the advancement of AI in complex IICGs.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Diagnose Machine Faults? A Comprehensive Survey from Deep Learning to Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis plays a central role in maintaining the reliability and safety of modern industrial systems. Over the past decade, deep learning methods-including convolutional neural networks, recurrent architectures, and generative adversarial networks-have substantially advanced diagnostic accuracy for rotating machinery, power systems, and manufacturing processes. More recently, large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a disruptive paradigm, offering capabilities in natural language reasoning, multimodal fusion, and few-shot generalization that complement or surpass conventional approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive survey tracing the evolution from traditional data-driven fault diagnosis through deep learning to the nascent adoption of LLMs and foundation models. We organize the literature into a structured taxonomy covering signal-level feature extraction, supervised and self-supervised deep architectures, transfer and meta-learning strategies, and LLM-based pipelines that integrate domain knowledge via prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and fine-tuning. A critical comparison of representative methods across standard benchmarks highlights the strengths and current limitations of each paradigm. We identify key open challenges-including domain-specific pretraining, realtime deployment, multimodal alignment, and interpretabilityand outline actionable research directions. By bridging the deep learning and LLM communities for industrial fault diagnosis, this review aims to accelerate progress toward more generalizable, explainable, and autonomous diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Natural Language to SQL at Scale: Integrating OpenAI with Oracle Autonomous Database via SELECT AI
papers.abstract: Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) translation has emerged as a critical capability for democratizing enterprise data access. We present one of the first independent empirical evaluations of Oracle Autonomous Database 26AI's SELECT AI feature, which leverages OpenAI GPT-4 to convert natural language into executable SQL. Using a custom evaluation framework and 22 TPC-H benchmark queries spanning simple, medium, and complex difficulty tiers, we measure SQL generation accuracy and end-to-end latency. Our results show an overall accuracy of 95.5% (90.9% exact SQL match), while mean end-to-end latency was 3,906ms, of which 94.5% is attributable to LLM generation overhead. The model demonstrated intelligent query optimization, selecting targeted columns over broad COUNT(*) patterns — a behavior not reflected in exact-match metrics. These findings establish a reproducible baseline for enterprise NL2SQL deployment and identify LLM generation as the primary optimization target. Code and dataset: myGitHubLink

papers.title: PITS-Net: A Physiological-Intensity and Topological Synergy Network for Joint Tumor-Vessel Co-segmentation
papers.abstract: Parotid tumors are highly invasive, often infiltrating adjacent blood vessels, nerves, and soft tissues. Integrating deep learning with Computed Tomography (CT) imaging for diagnosis and precise tumor-vessel co-segmentation is critical for surgery. However, existing methods fail to fully leverage CT information-such as physiological intensity (e.g., CT values) and tumorvessel topology-leading to underutilized dataset information and poor interpretability. To address this, we propose Physiological-Intensity and Topological Synergy Network (PITS-Net) for simultaneous and accurate segmentation of parotid tumors and adjacent vessels. Specifically, a Grouped Channel-Intensity Soft Attention (G-CISA) layer captures physiological intensity. And we integrate a Synergy Bridge Module into the encoder and design a Topological Synergy Mapping (TSM) for intermediate supervision using tumor-vessel topology to guide structural information use. A dual-stream decoder enables co-segmentation with TSM-guided spatial guidance and cross-stream refinement. Experiments conducted on a high-quality annotated private dataset demonstrate that PITS-Net achieves remarkably prominent performance. When extended to public datasets for liver tumor and vessel segmentation, the model also yields favorable results. These experimental findings verify that PITS-Net can deeply exploit the information inherent in datasets and exhibits excellent generalizability.

papers.title: Measuring Teaching Efficacy Through Comprehension Delta: Large Language Models as Standardized Learner Proxies
papers.abstract: Measuring teaching quality remains one of the most persistent challenges in educational research. Existing approaches depend on classroom observation protocols that require trained human raters, or on student evaluations that correlate poorly with actual learning outcomes. Both suffer from subjectivity, scalability constraints, and well-documented biases. This paper proposes a novel measurement construct, the dual-run comprehension delta, which reframes teaching efficacy as the measurable change in a standardized evaluator's comprehension before and after receiving a teacher's explanation. We argue that large language models can serve as controlled learner proxies for this purpose, and we develop a formal framework in which a domain-specific assessment is administered to an LLM twice: once without access to the teacher's explanation, and once with it. The score difference constitutes the delta. We ground this construct in established validity theory from the Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing, analyze it through the lens of pedagogical content knowledge and explanation quality research, and present a reference architecture that instantiates the methodology. We argue that the dual-run delta offers a reproducible and scalable complement to existing teaching quality measures, particularly suited for asynchronous instruction, teacher certification, and professional development contexts. We outline a validity argument organized around Kane's interpretation/use framework, discuss the construct boundaries of the approach, and identify the empirical studies required to evaluate its claims.

papers.title: Rediscovering Architectural Decision Records: How Persistent Design Context Improves LLM Code Generation
papers.abstract: As AI coding tools proliferate, multi-turn development using large language models (LLMs) is becoming commonplace. However, the "context degradation" problem-where design intent is lost across sessionsremains a serious challenge that leads to quality deterioration as projects grow in complexity. This study proposes "sqlew," a tool that repurposes Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)-a practice proposed in 2011 but abandoned due to human operational overhead-as external design memory for LLMs. sqlew realizes automated ADR recording and selective retrieval via structured queries through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), constructing a coexistence model of static instruction (CLAUDE.md) and dynamic rationale (ADR). We conducted a controlled experiment on a 12.5-turn TypeScript workflow approval system development across three conditions: no ADR (vanilla), from-inception adoption (sqlew), and retroactive adoption (Vanilla-to-sqlew, v2s). The sqlew condition reduced development time by 10.1% (496 min vs. 552 min) and total tool calls by 10.8%. In the vanilla condition, a supplementary turn (Turn 12.6: 29 min, 21,751K tokens) was required to compensate for missing E2E tests; including this hidden cost widened the time difference to 14.6%. Keyword-based density analysis of Chain of Thought (CoT) revealed a qualitative shift in reasoning patterns (Trial-and-Error Loop → Context-Informed Reasoning) and accelerating divergence in prior decision reference density (+21% → +64% → +137%). The most striking finding is the compliance gap between instruction and rationale. Despite the same TDD instruction being present in CLAUDE.md, conditions where ADRs contained the rationale for why TDD was adopted (sqlew/v2s) spontaneously generated 16-25 E2E tests, whereas the vanilla condition produced zero. LLMs exhibit higher compliance and reasoning quality toward "why to do something (rationale)" than "what to do (instruction)." We release all session logs, prompts, and analysis code, and invite replication.

papers.title: Assessing Small-Signal System Strength Across Modes, Locations and Operating Conditions for Inverter Based Resource Connections
papers.abstract: New sub-synchronous oscillations (SSO) have emerged in power systems with rises in connections of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs). This has prompted a search for better processes for identifying vulnerabilities to SSO during the planning of an IBR connection, recognising the features of IBRs, the modes to which they are vulnerable, and the heightened dependency on the operating point of the system. A metric named Admittance Margin (AM) is described, tailored to this problem, which evaluates small-signal system strength across several modes and locations and is used within a framework to explore operating point dependency. Suites of operating scenarios are developed systematically for an IBR-dominated test system based on historical demand and generation data. A procedure is defined to select the most critical operating points (COPs), to reduce the computational burden of performing system strength studies across all operating scenarios. Visualisation tools are provided to facilitate an effective interpretation of the AM results across multiple case studies so as to highlight where and when problematic conditions may occur.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for NLP Tasks by ReLabel Method
papers.abstract: In industry deep learning application, our dataset has a certain number of noisy data. The init datasets are from human labeling or LLM (large language model) generation or user behavior log. To solve this problem and achieve more than 90 score in dev dataset, we present a framework to find the noisy data and relabel the noisy data, given the model predictions as references in relabeling. The process of relabeling can be done manually or using LLM for annotation. In this paper, we illustrate our idea for a broad set of deep learning tasks, includes classification, sequence tagging, object detection, sequence generation, click-through rate prediction. The dev dataset evaluation results and human evaluation results verify our idea.

papers.title: A System-Level Framework for Sentiment-Aware Reflective Writing Systems: Modeling Temporal Emotional Patterns with Interpretability and Ethical Safety
papers.abstract: Sentiment analysis has become a cornerstone of affective computing applications, enabling systems to detect emotional valence in usergenerated text. However, when deployed in reflective writing and coaching contexts, sentiment-based systems face a fundamental limitation: sentiment polarity does not reliably indicate user intent, therapeutic need, or appropriate system response. This paper formally analyzes the gap between sentiment detection and intent interpretation in emotion-aware interactive systems. We define sentiment as a function S : X → Y s mapping text to polarity labels, and intent as a context-dependent function I : X × C × G × H → A incorporating conversational context, user goals, and interaction history. Through system-level observations from early-stage prototype deployment, we demonstrate that S(x) alone is statistically insufficient for determining appropriate system actions. We present a multi-layer intent modeling framework that augments sentiment detection with pragmatic reasoning, temporal pattern recognition, and goal-aware interpretation. Our central contribution is a utility-theoretic framing of emotional response selection that explicitly models asymmetric costs (false intervention vs. missed support), derives optimal decision thresholds, and incorporates ethical constraints through action-space restriction.

papers.title: Beyond Surface Affect: Why Sentiment Detection Alone is Insufficient for Intent Interpretation in Human-AI Communication
papers.abstract: Sentiment detection-the automated classification of affective polarity in natural language text-has achieved strong empirical performance across standard benchmarks and is widely deployed in conversational AI systems. However, in interactive Human-AI communication contexts such as interview coaching assistants, reflective writing platforms, and mental health dialogue agents, sentiment polarity alone is demonstrably insufficient for interpreting user intent. This paper formalizes the distinction between sentiment detection and intent interpretation using mathematical notation. We define a sentiment classifier S(x) operating over surface text and contrast it with a contextualized intent function I(x, C, G, H), where C denotes dialogue context, G encodes user goals, and H represents interaction history. We prove formally that S(x) does not imply I(x, C, G, H) in the general case, and identify four canonical failure modes of sentiment-only systems. We present system-level case observations from MindNook, a sentiment-aware reflective diary platform, to ground these theoretical distinctions empirically. We propose a Multi-Layer Intent Modeling (MLIM) framework integrating affective, pragmatic, goal-theoretic, and contextual components, and conclude with an open research agenda addressing context management, multi-modal grounding, and privacy-preserving personalization.

papers.title: K9-AIF: A Governed, Modular Framework for Agentic AI Applications
papers.abstract: Agentic systems increasingly combine multiple cooperating agents, heterogeneous models, and external tools, creating new challenges in governance, traceability, and architectural extensibility at enterprise scale. Existing orchestration frameworks often emphasize task coordination but provide limited support for consistent policy enforcement, observability, and long-term maintainability. This article presents a pattern-based architectural approach for governed agentic systems, grounded in a clear separation between Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs) and Solution Building Blocks (SBBs). Configuration-driven factories, runtime agent loaders, and layered architectural abstractions are used to structure orchestration, inference integration, persistence, and monitoring in a modular and governance-first manner. Diagrams illustrate how these elements compose into a cohesive architecture that supports extensibility while preserving stable architectural contracts.

papers.title: Blockchain-Enabled Infrastructure for Secure and Auditable AI Systems
papers.abstract: Security and auditability are critical requirements for AI systems deployed in enterprise and mission-critical environments. This article investigates how blockchain technology can be leveraged as an infrastructure component to enhance the security posture of AI systems. Using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) Dataset as a high-stakes case study, we propose a blockchain-enabled AI infrastructure that records cryptographic hashes of datasets, model parameters, and training accuracy, creating an immutable audit trail for AI operations. This approach enables post-hoc verification of AI behavior, supports forensic analysis, and strengthens compliance with emerging AI regulations and risk management frameworks. Our implementation demonstrates that anchoring a 98% accurate medical diagnostic model into a Vyper smart contract consumes approximately 110,472 gas, proving that forensic integrity is both technically and economically viable. The article discusses trade-offs, performance considerations, and potential integration patterns with cloud-native AI platforms.

papers.title: Joint Detection on Reconfigurable Photonic Processors with Multi-Input Phase Stabilization
papers.abstract: We report a joint-detection (JD) experiment between two reconfigurable photonic processors in which Hadamard codewords are generated on a transmitter processor and a Hadamard transform is performed on a receiver (decoder) processor. Crucially, the decoder executes multi-input phase stabilization concurrently with the optical Hadamard combining, ensuring the phase alignment required for coherent joint detection. We demonstrate JD using 2×2 and 4×4 Hadamard transformations and verify stable temporal outputs under active on-chip feedback control (FBC). The approach leverages our multi-input FBC scheme to suppress low-frequency inter-input phase fluctuations and to realize coherent combining consistent with Green-Machine style architectures. These results indicate a practical path to scalable, codeword-level optical joint detection on programmable photonic hardware and are compatible with larger-mode processors and higher-order code families.

papers.title: CSI-Free Deep Learning Based Hardware-Aware Precoding for Wideband Near-Field THz Systems
papers.abstract: This letter investigates hybrid analog precoding for wideband near-field terahertz (THz) ultra-massive multiple-input multiple-output (UM-MIMO) systems, considering the severe beam squint and hardware limitations of true time delay (TTD) elements and phase shifters (PSs). We formulate the joint optimization of TTD and PS coefficients as a non-convex mixedinteger problem subject to constraints on TTD range/resolution and PS quantization. To address this problem, we propose a hardware-aware unsupervised deep learning framework that operates directly in the measurement domain, avoiding explicit channel estimation at inference stage. The proposed framework incorporates a hardware-aware model-based loss function to maximize near-field array gain while enforcing TTD and PS constraints. Through this design, the framework learns a nonlinear mapping from carrier-frequency pilot measurements to hardware-compliant precoding coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance of the proposed framework over recent schemes under TTD and PS limitations.

papers.title: Vulnerability Assessment of Adversarial Image Attacks in a Miniaturized Autonomous Vehicle Testbed without Relying on Way-Point Information
papers.abstract: This paper presents a real-time perception and control framework to assess adversarial image attacks on an autonomous vehicle testbed. The system integrates 2D LiDAR with a YOLOv5n-based detector in a multithreaded architecture to execute a staged multi-stop navigation routine with turns and visual alignment before each stop. Baseline experiments show reliable operation without requiring way-point information, with consistent stopping accuracy and path completion across repeated runs. Instead of using traditional digital overlays, we evaluated our testbed on adversarial patterns on a physical traffic sign. To assess vulnerability against adversarial images, specific adversarial variants of traffic signs were tested. This cause marked reductions in detection range and even missed recognitions. To restore performance without changing sensing, fusion, or control, we apply adversarial learning to fine-tune YOLOv5n. The retrained model recovers detection reliability across all variants and returns the vehicle to normal closed-loop behavior without relying on waypoint information.

papers.title: stdio Bus: A Deterministic Kernel for Multi-Process Agent Transport
papers.abstract: Emerging agent protocols such as the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) require a transport layer that can multiplex NDJSON-framed JSON-RPC messages between external clients and worker processes while preserving session affinity. We present stdio Bus (implemented as Agent Transport OS, or stdio Bus kernel), a deterministic C11 runtime that provides exactly this capability. The system is single-threaded, uses only POSIX APIs and libc, and abstracts platform-specific I/O multiplexing (epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS) behind a unified event loop. stdio Bus kernel performs zero protocol interpretation: it extracts only the id, sessionId, and method fields from each message for routing, forwarding all bytes unchanged. Session-to-worker mapping uses round-robin assignment with affinity preservation; request-response correlation is tracked in a bounded pending-request table. Per-connection backpressure, bounded buffers, and a supervised restart policy with exponential backoff provide resource safety. We describe the architecture, the normative specification (RFC 2119 compliant), the worker contract, and the configuration schema. The system is intended as a foundational transport kernel: a reusable, protocol-agnostic substrate on which higher-level agent runtimes can be composed. We analyse the design trade-offs, enumerate known limitations-including hard-coded table sizes and the absence of TLS, authentication, and request timeouts-and outline directions for future work.

papers.title: VFS-Net: A Vertex and Face-Based Deep Learning Pipeline for Three-Dimensional Model Segmentation and Analysis
papers.abstract: This study presents a pipeline for the segmentation and analysis of dynamic, three-dimensional models using VFS-Net, a dual vertex- and face-based pipeline. This framework demonstrates favorable segmentation and classification metrics for both biological and synthetic 3D model types, demonstrating broad applicability. Benchmarking across diverse datasets demonstrates that VFS-Net remains robust against variations in model complexity and mesh density. Traditional machine learning methods require structured grids or volumetric data and are not optimized to handle data points that vary broadly based on scale and surface area. The VFS-Net pipeline was designed to operate on 3D models obtained using structured-light scanning, enabling the accurate capture of complex surface geometrics and topological features. Future extensions of this framework will further integrate two-dimensional data, extending its biomedical research relevance.

papers.title: Design of Frequency-PRT Coupled Agile Waveform and Low-Complexity Signal Processing
papers.abstract: Frequency-agile(FA) radars allow flexible changes in carrier frequency between adjacent pulses, offering significant advantages in anti-jamming performance. However, the discontinuity in echo phase renders the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) unsuitable, resulting in a high computational burden for coherent integration.To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Frequency-Pulse Repetition Time(PRT) Coupled Agile (FPCA) waveform design scheme, wherein the velocity-induced phase within a coherent processing interval (CPI) is constrained to be an integer multiple of a constant, thereby facilitating subsequent coherent integration. We first derive the analytical relationship between carrier frequency and PRT in FPCA, and then propose two FPCA design approaches: one with a constrained lower PRT bound, and another with both upper and lower PRT bounds.Furthermore, a fast signal processing method tailored for the proposed waveform in multi-target scenarios is developed.After phase cancellation of the echoes, the Velocity Spectrum Profile (VSP) is obtained via FFT, and multiple VSPs are non-coherently accumulated to suppress cross-terms arising from phase compensation, enabling robust estimation of strong target velocities.Velocity compensation and IFFT are then applied to obtain range estimates for strong targets, followed by weak target imaging based on the CLEAN algorithm.Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. Compared with existing coherent processing methods for frequency-agile radars, the proposed approach significantly reduces computational complexity, requiring only several to a dozen FFTs to obtain target parameter estimates, thus offering a practical frequency-agile solution for radar platforms with limited computational resources and stringent real-time requirements.

papers.title: LXB: A Route-Then-Act Framework for Cross-Device Mobile Automation via VLM-XML Fusion
papers.abstract: Mobile automation frameworks powered by vision-language models (VLMs) suffer from high latency, excessive API costs, and poor reliability on complex multi-page tasks. We present LXB, a crossdevice mobile automation framework that addresses these limitations through a hybrid neuro-symbolic architecture. LXB introduces three core innovations: (1) VLM-XML Fusion, which aligns semantic detections from VLMs with structural XML accessibility nodes through point-containment matching; (2) Route-Then-Act paradigm, which separates deterministic graph-based navigation from AI-guided execution; and (3) Node-Driven Exploration, which constructs navigation graphs through breadth-first traversal of discovered navigation nodes. Our evaluation on 8 real-world tasks across Taobao and Bilibili achieves an overall success rate of 100%. On deep tasks requiring ≥2 navigation hops, LXB achieves 100% success with only 1.0 model call-a single LLM query during the planning phase-compared to VLM-ReAct's 80.0% with 3.87 model calls: a 74% reduction in model invocations and 58.6% reduction in token consumption.

papers.title: The Rise of the Agentic Era: Quantifying the Shift from Chatbots to Autonomous Security
papers.abstract: The security landscape is quickly changing As LLMs evolve into autonomous agents. A scientometric analysis of 22,416 papers reveals that Autonomous Vulnerability Discovery has increased 9.6× since 2023, now exceeding secure code generation and indicating a shift from static safeguards to more dynamic cyber-defense approaches.

papers.title: Minimum Cost Encoding for Coded Distributed Computing Systems
papers.abstract: In large-scale distributed matrix-vector multiplications, e.g., for generative AI, straggling nodes can slow down or even jeopardize the whole operation. Coded distributed computing (CDC) uses erasure codes to create redundant computations and combat stragglers. This requires encoding very large matrices. Moreover, encoding must be repeated whenever system parameters (e.g., weight matrices in AI models) evolve. This paper introduces a general framework for reducing encoding complexity in CDC. We propose the notion of an encoding blueprint, a construction schedule that specifies how each coded symbol is constructed from data and previously computed coded symbols. An optimal blueprint minimizes the number of arithmetic operations required for a given code. We first design blueprints using addition-only operations. We then extend the framework to also allow subtraction, which further decreases the number of required operations. The optimization problem is cast as a mixed-integer program (MIP), and solved. Numerical results on matrix-vector multiplication show that optimized blueprints reduce encoding operations by up to 60 percent compared to standard methods, saving billions of operations in large-scale applications. Our techniques can be used for efficient decoding as well.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Adversarial Attacks on Model Utility, Privacy, and Explainability: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems are now central to many real-world applications, but their growing adoption has also increased their exposure to diverse adversarial threats. This survey proposes a unified multidimensional threat model that organizes attacks according to attacker knowledge, objectives, specificity, capabilities, and lifecycle phase. Unlike existing surveys that focus mainly on utility-harmed and privacy-harmed attacks, our framework also covers explainability-harmed attacks. We present a comprehensive taxonomy, a comparison table summarizing the properties of representative attacks, and a lifecycle-based view showing how they occur from pre-training to inference. We further analyze emerging adversarial risks in machine learning models, including federated and continual learning, and discuss open challenges and research directions for building robust and trustworthy machine learning systems.

papers.title: A Survey of Unifying Large Language Models with Graph Learning: Concepts, Methods, and Recent Advancements for Text-attributed Graph
papers.abstract: Graphs are ubiquitous and have been used in a wide range of applications. Before the rise of large language models (LLMs), graph neural networks (GNNs) were among the most popular methods for graph learning. Techniques such as node embedding, graph convolution, graph attention, and random walkbased methods have been widely adopted. When handling graphs with textual node attributes, shallow text embeddings are typically used as initial node representations. However, these embeddings often capture only limited general knowledge. In recent years, LLMs have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing, opening new opportunities for handling text data. In this survey, we explore how to leverage LLMs for graph machine learning. We focus on different types of tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph-based question answering. Specifically, we investigate two main approaches: LLMs as Enhancers and LLMs as Predictors. In the first approach, LLMs enrich node textual attributes with their vast knowledge, after which graph learning methods are used to make predictions. In the second approach, graph data is treated as input for LLMs, which directly solve various graph-related tasks. Through a thorough investigation of these two directions, we share observations and new insights on integrating LLMs with graph learning.

papers.title: A Survey of (Deep RAG) Deep Retrieval Augmented Generation and Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for combining large language models with external knowledge sources to produce accurate, context-aware, and verifiable outputs. In this survey, we focus on an advanced instantiation of this paradigm, referred to as Deep RAG, which integrates reasoning, memory, and multi-step planning into end-to-end research workflows. We provide a structured overview of Deep RAG systems, covering key components such as query planning, information retrieval, memory management, and answer generation, as well as practical optimization techniques including supervised fine-tuning, iterative self-evolving, and agentic reinforcement learning. We analyze different planning strategies, adaptive retrieval mechanisms, conflict resolution methods, and multimodal synthesis, highlighting both their strengths and limitations. By categorizing approaches according to workflow types, reasoning strategies, and optimization paradigms, we clarify the current landscape and identify open challenges for evaluation, scalability, and multimodal reasoning. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive roadmap for designing flexible, reliable, and intelligent Deep RAG systems capable of performing complex, real-world research tasks with minimal human supervision.

papers.title: FedDroneQ: A Quantized Federated YOLOv5 Framework for Efficient UAV Object Detection
papers.abstract: This paper presents FedDroneQ, a reproducible federated learning framework that adapts the YOLOv5 detector for privacy-preserving and communication-efficient UAV object detection. FedDroneQ trains lightweight YOLOv5s models on distributed VisDrone subsets and compresses client-to-server updates using 8-bit symmetric quantization. To mitigate statistical heterogeneity across UAV clients, the framework supports Dirichlet non-IID partitioning and incorporates a FedProx-style proximal regularizer. Beyond the core algorithm, FedDroneQ writes auditable artifacts to disk (configuration, per-round communication accounting, and update-norm summaries) and exposes diagnostic probes for localization and prediction behavior. Our experiments emphasize reproducible end-to-end validation, including CUDA runs that yield non-zero training/evaluation losses and non-zero update norms, confirming that federated rounds perform real parameter updates. We also report a small-subset detectionaccuracy sanity check using TorchMetrics mAP on a capped 200-image evaluation.

papers.title: Two-Gate Adaptive Context Selection: A Training-Free Framework for Efficient Document Filtering in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems frequently retrieve noisy document sets that dilute context quality and inflate inference costs. While recent approaches employ auxiliary language models or learned filters, they introduce computational overhead incompatible with production latency requirements. We present Two-Gate Adaptive Context Selection, a deterministic, training-free filtering algorithm that operates in O(N) time with submillisecond latency. Our method combines: (1) a safety trigger ensuring graceful degradation, (2) a purely relative threshold adapting to query-specific score distributions, and (3) a metric-aligned floor to prevent over-aggressive filtering. We validate on a suite of three diverse public benchmarks from BEIR (NFCorpus, SciFact, FiQA) covering medical, scientific, and financial domains, alongside a production dataset of 487 queries with 5,995 humanannotated relevance judgments. On all public benchmarks, Two-Gate matches the saturation quality of Top-10/Top-20 baselines exactly (NDCG differences < 0.0001) while halving context size. On production data, it achieves 96% context reduction compared to the unfiltered retrieval set (140.5 → 5.7 documents) and 69% reduction compared to a strong Top-20 baseline (18.2 → 5.7), while maintaining statistically identical quality (p > 0.05). Unlike Self-RAG or Cluster-based Adaptive Retrieval, Two-Gate is parameter-free and adds only 0.03ms latency. The deterministic logic of the Two-Gate algorithm is detailed herein, facilitating straightforward integration into production RAG frameworks.

papers.title: The Cognitive Fingerprint: LLM-Resistant Cross-Domain Threat Actor Attribution via Temporal-Syntactic Fusion
papers.abstract: The attribution of state-sophisticated threat actors across disjointed domains; linking overt "Surface Web" personas to covert "Dark Web" identities, remains a critical unsolved challenge in Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) [1][2]. Current State-of-the-Art (SOTA) frameworks, including transformer-based approaches such as De-Anonymization at Scale (DAS) [3], rely heavily on semantic features (BERT [4], RoBERTa), rendering them vulnerable to adversarial "style transfer" attacks where actors employ Large Language Models (LLMs) or automated translation to systematically scrub lexical fingerprints [5][6][7]. We term this capability ceiling the "LLM Wall": the point at which semantic attribution accuracy degrades to near-random probability against adversarially obfuscated text. This paper proposes a novel framework that bypasses the LLM Wall entirely by replacing Semantic Analysis with Behavioral Signal Processing. We introduce two complementary attribution modalities: (1) Logical Time-Difference-of-Arrival (L-TDoA), which adapts signal propagation mathematics from Electronic Warfare [8][9] to measure Cognitive Latency: the user-specific delay between Global Information Events and cross-platform reactions; and (2) SynGNN, a content-blind Graph Neural Network [10] that learns identity from Deep Syntactic Embeddings (dependency tree structures, POS-tag transitions [11]) rather than vocabulary, rendering it immune to lexical obfuscation. We evaluate these modalities through a Hybrid Validation Protocol comprising four components: (a) a scaled Enron-Reddit proxy corpus (200 user pairs) with adversarial stripping, (b) evaluation on the PAN 2020 Authorship Verification shared task [12] as a standard benchmark, (c) a 100,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation for L-TDoA stress-testing, and (d) a Retrospective Case Study applying the framework to publicly documented attribution cases (USA v. Ulbricht [13]; USA v. Netyksho et al. [14]). Results demonstrate that SynGNN recovers 78.6% (95% CI: 75.4-81.8%) of identities under full structural stripping conditions where BERT-based models collapse to 12.4%. An ablation study confirms that each modality contributes independently, with fusion yielding a simulated composite precision of 91.7% (95% CI: 88.3-94.1%) in controlled adversarial settings with 200 candidate suspects. We position this as a foundational framework at TRL 3, providing the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) with a resilient, physics-based attribution capability that addresses gaps identified by IARPA's SoURCE CODE [15], ReSCIND [16], and HIATUS [17] programs.

papers.title: SafeDD: A Mask-and-Retrain Defense Framework for Backdoor Mitigation in Dataset Distillation
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation has emerged as a promising technique to compress large-scale datasets into small synthetic sets, significantly reducing training overhead. However, this paradigm introduces a critical security vulnerability: malicious providers can embed hidden backdoors into the distilled data, causing downstream models to misclassify triggered inputs. Defending against such attacks in the distillation setting presents a unique challenge due to the extreme scarcity of synthetic samples (e.g., 10 images per class). Conventional defenses, which rely on filtering or discarding suspicious samples, fail in this regime as removing high-density samples leads to a catastrophic collapse in model utility. To address this dilemma, we propose SafeDD, a novel defense framework based on a Mask-andRetrain strategy. Our approach formulates an optimization objective to decouple and extract dominant features from synthetic images. We optimize a mask to eliminate these influential features and subsequently retrain the model to evaluate the impact. The core insight leverages the shortcut learning phenomenon: we posit that the dominant features in poisoned samples converge to the backdoor trigger, whereas in benign samples, they correspond to critical semantic content. Consequently, masking these features effectively neutralizes the backdoor in poisoned classes while retaining sufficient semantic information for classification. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SafeDD successfully reduces the attack success rate to near 0% and maintains robust recognition accuracy on the targeted malicious classes.

papers.title: Motivating Mundane Tasks Through AR Gamification
papers.abstract: Mundane household tasks are easy to procrastinate, partly because common motivation tools (e.g., reminders) decouple from the phys ical context where the task happens. We explore whether situated augmented reality (AR) gamification can make a simple cleaning task feel more engaging and motivating when incentives embed directly into the workspace. We built a Meta Quest AR prototype that lets users define a cleaning region and “collect” virtual coins within that region via hand tracking, with real-time HUD progress and audio feedback. We evaluated the system in a within-subjects, counterbalanced study (N = 15) comparing the same wiping task with and without AR, measuring completion time and collecting Likert-scale and open-ended feedback on engagement, motivation, fun, usability, and adoption intent. Results suggest AR meaning fully improves subjective experience (e.g., engagement increased from 3.13 to 4.42, with higher motivation and fun), while not sig nificantly improving objective performance (cleaning time) or per ceived speed/efficiency/ease of use. Qualitative responses indicate a core tension: virtual rewards can increase enjoyment but may distract from task goals when rewards are misaligned with actual dirt and when setup friction is nontrivial. These findings provide empirical evidence that situated AR gamification can enhance the subjective experience of mundane chores in a single-session setting, while highlighting design constraints—reward-task alignment and low-friction setup—that likely govern whether motivational gains translate into effective real-world use.
